messages:
alice: Deploybot blocked canary for release v0.34.1 :warning: SBOM signature missing for container image and scan surfaced a transitive CVE (low) in third-party lib (libfoo 1.2.3). Holding rollout.

deploybot: [automated] canary-quarantine: reason=sbom_unverified; scan_flag=transitive_cve: LIBFOO-2025-1234; severity=low; affected: edge-canary-eu

mike: noted. is the missing signature for the build or the base image? quick grep shows IMAGE_SHA present but signature metadata empty.

jenny: base image unsigned. builder pipeline uploaded SBOM but cosign verify failed due to missing key. pipeline logs: `cosign verify -key $KMS_URI image:sha256:...` -> exit 1

sre-oncall: we have 2 options: (A) pin to previous vetted base image and resume canary, (B) stop rollout and request signed SBOM from infra, (C) if security ok with low transitive CVE, we can opt for a limited canary in non-prod regions. what's the risk tolerance for this release window?

security: quick triage: LIBFOO-2025-1234 is low and transitive via dep chain. No exploit seen in telemetry. But unsigned SBOM is a separate compliance issue — Legal will want evidence for prod. We can't just gloss over signature absence for enterprise customers.

legal: correct, unsigned SBOM triggers compliance checklist fail. We can permit a timeboxed exception for internal-only canaries or non-customer-facing rollout with clear remediation plan. For prod-facing canary we need either signature or formal exception logged.

alice: release is mostly bugfixes and one doc change. Preference: get signature or pin base image. How long to pin and re-run validations?

mike: pin is fastest. I can update the manifest to base@sha256:<prevsha> and trigger a rebuild; should be ~25-30m to produce signed artifact if pipeline picks up the right key.

jenny: if we pin, please ensure the change is recorded in release notes and call out the pin reason. Also we should add a telemetry flag to watch for any regressions.

sre-oncall: propose this plan: pin base image -> run pipeline -> verify cosign -> re-run sbom + vuln scan -> lift canary hold. Timebox: 2 hours. If any step fails, rollback to manual hold and escalate.

security: agree with plan. Also add a follow-up ticket to fix key propagation in builder: DEVEXP-3456.

legal: we accept timeboxed limited canary once SBOM signed. Document exception in compliance log. I'll stamp approval once I see signature artifact.

alice: ok mike, go ahead. mike: starting now. ping here when cosign passes.

mike: updated manifest, kicked rebuild at `ci/2026-03-20/4578`. cosign check in progress. :eyes:

deploybot: [automated] build-started ci/2026-03-20/4578

mike: cosign verify -> success. SBOM signature attached. re-running vuln scan.

deploybot: [automated] scan-complete: no new high/critical findings; transitive low still present (LIBFOO-2025-1234). canary release UNBLOCKED for edge-canary-eu.

alice: lifting hold. proceeding with limited canary per plan. watchers: security, legal, sre.

sre-oncall: monitoring windows open for 4h. set rollback criteria: error spike >2x baseline or latency p50 >200ms for any route.

jenny: adding release note line: "Pinned base image due to SBOM signature propagation issue; full rollout will resume after infra key fix (DEVEXP-3456)."

legal: recorded exception: EXC-2026-104. good to proceed. :white_check_mark:

mike: rolling to canary now. /deploy start edge-canary-eu v0.34.1

deploybot: [automated] deploy-started user=mike target=edge-canary-eu release=v0.34.1

alice: thanks everyone. follow-up: schedule a postmortem on key propagation and add a note in the changelog about pinned base for traceability. :thumbsup:
